description.value: The study examined whether anodal tDCS over the left inferior frontal gyrus, paired with language therapy, altered resting-state functional connectivity and whether connectivity changes were associated with improvements in written naming in primary progressive aphasia.

spans.text: This is an analysis of the first phase results of the current clinical trial, focusing on the association between gains in written naming (the primary outcome measure) and changes in connectivity in participants who initially received tDCS versus those who initially received sham.

design.value: A double-blinded, within-subject crossover clinical trial was analyzed using only the first phase, with a between-subject comparison of participants initially assigned to anodal tDCS plus speech-language therapy versus sham plus speech-language therapy.

spans.text: Participants belonged to a larger cohort who received tDCS and sham (plus language therapy) in a double-blinded, within-subject crossover design (see Clinical Trial Identifier: NCT02606422 on clinicaltrials.gov ).

Given the complexity of modeling a possible carryover effect with the additional effect of neurodegeneration and the unknown effect of an adequate wash-out period in neurodegenerative diseases, we focus on data only from the first phase of stimulation in a between-subject design.

The proxy we used to measure performance in written naming was letter accuracy instead of whole-word accuracy because we wanted to capture more subtle changes at the graphemic level as well as the letter-sound correspondences, i.e., to capture changes in both the lexical and sublexical representation of each word.

description.value: Percentage of correct letters corresponding to sounds making up words, scored with a rule-based system and used as the primary outcome.

spans.text: language treatment test scores (letter accuracy, i.e., percentage of letters corresponding to sounds making up words) were collected before and after the written naming/spelling treatment intervention, with percentage of correct letters as the primary outcome.

The primary outcomes for the present study were changes in written naming because writing has the potential to be a good compensatory mechanism for alternative communication in cases of oral language decline in some PPA variants, as exemplified in the introduction.

2.3 Written word production/spelling intervention

task_description.value: An oral and written picture naming and spelling therapy using a spell-study-spell procedure, with semantic cues, corrective feedback, and repeated practice of trained words.

spans.text: In particular, we used the same picture for oral and written naming.
Each patient was given a set of 10–30 words for practice during the treatment.

spans.text: we focus on data only from the first phase of stimulation in a between-subject design.

instructions.value: The patient was shown a picture on the computer, asked to orally name the object, and then write it down.

spans.text: In detail, each training trial, the patient was shown a picture on the computer, asked to orally name the object, and then write it down.

stimuli.value: Pictures of objects and trained and untrained words; each patient practiced a set of 10–30 words.

spans.text: There were two sets of materials: trained items (practiced at each session of either tDCS or sham stimulation), and untrained items (not practiced but only tested before treatment and at follow-up points).

spans.text: The resting-state fMRI was also processed in MRICloud and analyzed in a seed-by-seed manner.

The MRICloud pipeline follows well established steps for rsfMRI processing: after exclusion of “outlier” TRs, detected by ART routine (parameters: 2 standard deviations for motion and 4 standard deviations for intensity, more severe than the default of 9), the movement matrix combined with the physiological nuisance matrix is used in the deconvolution regression for the remaining TRs.
